name: Joed
overview: Joed is a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Pedaiah. His mention in Nehemiah 11:7 highlights his place within the post-exilic community of Israel. No additional personal details or notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Joed means 'y-h-v-h is witness,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the Lord as a witness. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 11:7, is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries significant spiritual meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Joed as the son of Pedaiah and infers Meshullam as his father, situating him within a known family line. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Joed's significance lies in his inclusion among the people of Benjamin who resettled Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. His genealogy affirms the restoration of the tribe and the continuity of God's covenant people. Though not a prominent figure in narrative events, his presence underscores the faithfulness of God in preserving His people through generations.
